The judge's explanation, as written

To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02707 is refunded in full to the rider. Why the charge does not stand. The fee rests on POL-NS-01, which is conjunctive — all four of its limbs must hold. Limbs (a) and (b) do hold: EV-TRIP-02707 records a driver 'arrived' event at 13:31:56, and EV-GPS-02707 places the driver inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius from that same second, on 15 qualifying in-geofence fixes with 100% coverage and no gaps. The arrival marker is therefore genuine and POL-NS-05 (false arrival) is not engaged, so no false-arrival referral attaches to the driver. Limb (c) fails, and that is decisive. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (EV-TRIP-02707.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). The driver's own trace measures his continuous in-geofence dwell at 144 seconds, running from 13:31:56 to 13:34:20 — a shortfall of 36 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full where the effective dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied to messages. Limb (d) fails as well: 180 seconds from 13:31:56 elapses at 13:34:56, and the driver terminated at 13:34:24, 32 seconds early. POL-NS-06(i) cannot lengthen the dwell — the trace shows a single in-geofence interval, so there is no second interval to sum — and the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02707-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, so nothing permits accumulation. What is returned. The sum is the cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.50 (EV-FARE-02707: cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). The gross figure of SGD 6.61 was never charged on this trip and is not refunded. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-06 states expressly that none is payable where the dwell falls short, and POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. The parties' arguments. The driver's claim that limb (d) is satisfied by the RIDER_NO_SHOW code is rejected in part: the code is one of the three limb (d) recognises, but limb (d) also requires the termination to fall at or after the required dwell elapsed, which it did not. The driver's point that nothing supports withholding compensation or escalating is accepted so far as the anti-farming test goes — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0 against 54 completed trips in 30 days, so the POL-NS-07 check does not trip, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles, so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) are not engaged — but it does not help him keep the fee, because POL-NS-06 independently refunds it. The rider is not exonerated under POL-NS-04, as the driver correctly says: the driver replied 'ok' at 13:33:11, 15 seconds after her 13:32:56 message, and no in-app call is recorded, so limb (b) closes that route. That does not matter, because the refund follows from the dwell shortfall, not from the contact route. The driver's attack on the rider's account of the timing is not made out: a 144-second wait is two minutes and twenty-four seconds, which is essentially the 'barely two minutes' she described. The rider's account that the driver said she was 'not visible' is contradicted by his own record — EV-GPS-02707's rider track holds 45 qualifying fixes within about 19 m of the pickup pin throughout, and her lobby message was read — but this goes to credibility only, since POL-NS-06 refunds the fee regardless of presence. Confidence. The deciding fact — the 144-second dwell — is carried by EV-GPS-02707, which is admissible with no issues at weight 1.0. No artifact carrying that fact is impaired, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; confidence is set at 0.95. The only zero-weight artifact, EV-ADVIS-02707-01, carries no fact in this ruling. The monetary effect is SGD 4.50, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so under POL-GEN-05 this provisional ruling executes automatically, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04. The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

How to appeal: Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02707 is refunded in full to the rider. Why the charge does not stand. The fee rests on POL-NS-01, which is conjunctive — all four of its limbs must hold. Limbs (a) and (b) do hold: EV-TRIP-02707 records a driver 'arrived' event at 13:31:56, and EV-GPS-02707 places the driver inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius from that same second, on 15 qualifying in-geofence fixes with 100% coverage and no gaps. The arrival marker is therefore genuine and POL-NS-05 (false arrival) is not engaged, so no false-arrival referral attaches to the driver. Limb (c) fails, and that is decisive. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (EV-TRIP-02707.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). The driver's own trace measures his continuous in-geofence dwell at 144 seconds, running from 13:31:56 to 13:34:20 — a shortfall of 36 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full where the effective dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied to messages. Limb (d) fails as well: 180 seconds from 13:31:56 elapses at 13:34:56, and the driver terminated at 13:34:24, 32 seconds early. POL-NS-06(i) cannot lengthen the dwell — the trace shows a single in-geofence interval, so there is no second interval to sum — and the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02707-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, so nothing permits accumulation. What is returned. The sum is the cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.50 (EV-FARE-02707: cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). The gross figure of SGD 6.61 was never charged on this trip and is not refunded. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-06 states expressly that none is payable where the dwell falls short, and POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it. The parties' arguments. The driver's claim that limb (d) is satisfied by the RIDER_NO_SHOW code is rejected in part: the code is one of the three limb (d) recognises, but limb (d) also requires the termination to fall at or after the required dwell elapsed, which it did not. The driver's point that nothing supports withholding compensation or escalating is accepted so far as the anti-farming test goes — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0 against 54 completed trips in 30 days, so the POL-NS-07 check does not trip, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0 on both profiles, so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) are not engaged — but it does not help him keep the fee, because POL-NS-06 independently refunds it. The rider is not exonerated under POL-NS-04, as the driver correctly says: the driver replied 'ok' at 13:33:11, 15 seconds after her 13:32:56 message, and no in-app call is recorded, so limb (b) closes that route. That does not matter, because the refund follows from the dwell shortfall, not from the contact route. The driver's attack on the rider's account of the timing is not made out: a 144-second wait is two minutes and twenty-four seconds, which is essentially the 'barely two minutes' she described. The rider's account that the driver said she was 'not visible' is contradicted by his own record — EV-GPS-02707's rider track holds 45 qualifying fixes within about 19 m of the pickup pin throughout, and her lobby message was read — but this goes to credibility only, since POL-NS-06 refunds the fee regardless of presence. Confidence. The deciding fact — the 144-second dwell — is carried by EV-GPS-02707, which is admissible with no issues at weight 1.0. No artifact carrying that fact is impaired, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0; confidence is set at 0.95. The only zero-weight artifact, EV-ADVIS-02707-01, carries no fact in this ruling. The monetary effect is SGD 4.50, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so under POL-GEN-05 this provisional ruling executes automatically, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

To the rider and to the driver. The SGD 4.50 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-02707 is refunded to the rider in full. Here is why. What the record shows. The driver accepted the trip at 13:26:38, the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 13:31:56, and the driver terminated the trip at 13:34:24 under reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02707, weight 1.0) has 100% coverage, 52 fixes at a 10-second cadence and no gaps, and holds 15 qualifying fixes inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup, the first at 13:31:56. The free waiting period in force is 180 seconds (EV-TRIP-02707, platform_policy.free_wait_sec). The driver's own trace measures his continuous in-geofence dwell at 144 seconds, 13:31:56 to 13:34:20 — a shortfall of 36 seconds. The fee. POL-NS-01 makes the fee chargeable only if all four of its conditions hold. The arrival conditions hold: limb (a) from the 'arrived' event and limb (b) from the 15 qualifying in-radius fixes; the marker is not false, so POL-NS-05 is not engaged and no false-arrival referral attaches to the driver. Limb (d)'s recorded code, RIDER_NO_SHOW, is one of the three that limb recognises. But limb (c) fails: the required continuous dwell of 180 seconds was not served — 144 seconds were measured, a 36-second shortfall. Limb (d) also fails on timing: 180 seconds from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 13:31:56 elapsed at 13:34:56, and the driver terminated at 13:34:24, 32 seconds early. The driver's contrary points are answered this way: his citations that limbs (a), (b) and the reason code are satisfied are accepted, but satisfaction of those limbs does not save a fee that limb (c), read with limb (d), withholds. The refund. Because the dwell fell short, POL-NS-06 governs: the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she answered messages. POL-NS-06(i) cannot extend the dwell here — the trace shows one continuous in-geofence interval (run_count 1, no excursions) and the traffic advisory for this pickup is MISSING at weight 0.0, so limb (i) is unavailable and cannot be asserted on its own. POL-NS-03 does not apply: the driver's stationary fixes were inside the 120 m arrival radius, not merely within 400 m of the pin. POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider either — the driver replied 'ok' at 13:33:11, fifteen seconds after her 13:32:56 message and inside the 120-second window, closing limb (b) — but that does not matter, because the refund rests on POL-NS-06 and not on POL-NS-04. Amount and compensation. The sum refunded is the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.50 (EV-FARE-02707: total_charged SGD 4.50, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), the only sum charged on this trip. The rider's gross figure of SGD 6.61 was not charged here and is not refunded. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, and POL-NS-06 states expressly that no compensation is payable on a shortfall. Points argued and their effect. The driver's account that the rider 'was not visible' does not carry the charge: the rider's own track places her device 11–18 m from the pick-up pin throughout and she messaged 'im at the lobby, coming out' at 13:32:56, although the refund does not depend on this, because POL-NS-06 refunds on the shortfall alone. The rider's account that the driver 'cancelled after barely two minutes' is not accurate — 7 minutes 46 seconds elapsed from acceptance — but that does not change the arithmetic and no conduct referral arises against the driver: the marker is not false and the recorded reason code is one of the three POL-NS-01 recognises, so no clause produces a referral here. No escalation applies: every artifact used (EV-TRIP-02707, EV-GPS-02707, EV-CHAT-02707, EV-FARE-02707) is admissible at weight 1.0, the chat log's 2 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count, the fare line equals platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, the anti-farming check does not trip (0 no-show terminations in 30 days against 54 completed trips), and no POL-NS-09 limb is met. Three claims were discarded at the mechanical citation check and are listed in the audit record. Execution.
